_doc: Revert-verify mutant for the IN-JEST half of issue #4444: after dropping `process.exit(0)` from `set-property`'s success path, every success axis asserts `expectNaturalExit` (exit was never called) instead of `toContain(0)` / `toEqual([0])` / `toBe(0)`. That predicate is what keeps the fix from being silently reverted by a future edit — restoring the exit reddens the axes below. ⚤ The DELIVERED-bytes half cannot live here (jest mocks process.stderr.write and process.exit, so no pipe and no flush is exercised — integration-test-revert-verify §A66); it lives in dryrun-4444.setproperty.spec.json. Same shape as set-body-4436.guard.spec.json, which locked the equivalent predicate for `set-body` in #4443. Expectation written BEFORE the run. Axis keys come from THIS suite because its test names carry machine-readable ids (N1, N1d, N2, N3, N3b); the other set-property suites use prose names, so their redness is visible as a failing suite but not extractable by red_re (integration-test-revert-verify §A47 — the axis NAME is the machine key).

M1_process_exit_restored._note: Restores process.exit(0) at the end of the success path. Every migrated success axis asserts that NO exit was recorded, so all of them redden at once — which is the point: the predicate is a ratchet against the exit coming back, not a per-scenario check.
